speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are having difficulty conceiving and experiencing discomfort during sexual activity; to help you, I will need to ask you some specific questions about your symptoms and history.

Have you and your partner been trying to conceive for more than a year, and can you describe exactly where and how the pain occurs during intercourse?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia secondary to pelvic floor dysfunction.

Based on your history of 15 months of trying to conceive and the specific report of pelvic floor muscle tension during penetration, I am considering a diagnosis of dyspareunia related to pelvic floor dysfunction. Given your history of body dysmorphic disorder, psychological factors may also be contributing, but we must first rule out organic causes. Would you be willing to undergo a pelvic floor physical examination and a vaginal ultrasound to evaluate for endometriosis or anatomical abnormalities?
